claims.statement: When a webhook is established, Asana sends a shared secret once in the X-Hook-Secret header of the handshake request; it is used afterwards to compute the SHA-256 HMAC signature (X-Hook-Signature) over webhook delivery bodies, and is not returned again when fetching the webhook.

sources.supports: Included in the header of that `POST` request from Asana is an `X-Hook-Secret`. This value serves as a shared secret that both Asana and the receiving server store.
Note that `X-Hook-Secret` is not returned again when fetching the webhook subscription object

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.

The webhooks page shows an example handshake value, but no sentence states that real secrets share its length or alphabet; the example is not recorded and a provider example does not prove a rule.
